title: Fitting a line by least squares
summary: Write least squares from the normal equations, then judge the fit.

milestones.title: The fit
milestones.explainBack: Explain why the normal equations give the line with the smallest squared error.

milestones.title: Goodness of fit
milestones.brief: Write `r_squared(x, y)`: the fraction of the variance in `y` that your line explains. A perfect fit gives 1; a flat line through the mean gives 0.
milestones.explainBack: Explain what r² measures, and one way a fit can have a high r² and still be the wrong model.

milestones.title: Errors in both variables
milestones.brief: Brief only, for now: when `x` is noisy too, ordinary least squares is biased toward a flatter slope. Look up total least squares and try it on the data from M1.
